subject: Data locus & conditional deployment clarifications
thread_text:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@meditech.eu>
To: Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.eu>; vanessa_ortiz
Cc: Kenji Sato <k.sato@nippon-health.jp>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:12:00 +0200
Subject: Question: EU residency + temporary APAC processing allowance

Hi Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the RFP response packet. A couple of clarifications from our security and procurement teams:

1) For production traffic originating in the EU, can you commit to processing both input and persisted output exclusively within EU-hosted infrastructure (no cross-border egress) for all customer-controlled data?

2) Meditech has a small set of non-PHI telemetry and model-cache warm-up jobs that run near APAC endpoints (Japan). Would Redwood consider a temporary exception to route only ephemeral cache/preprocessing for those jobs to APAC (Tokyo) provided the payloads are explicitly marked non-sensitive and TTL is <24 hours? We need your control model and logging guarantees documented.

3) If EU capacity is temporarily constrained, what automated fallback behavior exists and what are the contractual commitments (SLA/notice) required to route calls to other regions?

Please include any attestation artifacts you can share.

Thanks,
Anna
Procurement Lead, Meditech AG

---
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.company>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@meditech.eu>
Cc: ben_carter; stephanie_nguyen; Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.eu>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: EU residency + temporary APAC processing allowance

Anna,

Appreciate the clear questions — below is a concise summary and I'll attach supporting artifacts. TL;DR: Yes to exclusive EU processing for customer-controlled data when you select an EU-bound deployment (hosted or private). Temporary APAC exception for ephemeral, non-sensitive cache can be accommodated under strict controls and documented opt-in. Automated fallback to compatible model variants is available with notice and configurable policies; we describe the contractual options below.

1) EU-only processing and data at rest:
- Hosted EU option: When you configure the account region to EU, all inference requests, KV cache, and persisted outputs are routed to our EU data centers (Frankfurt, Amsterdam) and stored on EU-resident storage.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) option: You can choose a private deployment in your VPC or our on-prem bundle — in this mode, all compute and storage remain under your control and we do not egress.
- Controls: Encrypted at rest (AES-256), per-customer KMS key option (customer-managed, bring-your-own-key) and audit logs. We attach an attestation (redwood_region_attestation_q3_2027.pdf) with POPs and data flow diagrams.

2) Temporary APAC processing for ephemeral cache/preprocessing:
- Scope: Allowed only for artifacts you explicitly mark as non-sensitive (no PHI, no user identifiable data).
- TTL: Objects must be configured with TTL <= 24 hours; system enforces automatic purge.
- Isolation: Ephemeral caches are segregated from persisted outputs; keys for cache entries are ephemeral and rotated.
- Logging & evidence: All such requests are routed under a customer opt-in flag and produce searchable audit entries (timestamp, originating region, request hash, route decision).
- Approvals: Requires written zone-exception enrollment and a short SOW amendment; we can provide a SOC-style evidence packet for the change window.

3) Fallback behavior and contractual commitments:
- Default policy: Smart routing prefers EU capacity; if capacity is constrained we route to the nearest compatible EU site or can fail-fast based on latency SLOs if you opt-out of cross-region routing.
- Cross-region fallback: If you enable fallback, we route to a compatible model in US-East or APAC depending on policy. We recommend a tiered fallback list (EU->EU-burst->US-East).
- Notice & controls: For automatic cross-region fallback we provide: (a) pre-activation notice in console; (b) customer notification via API/webhook; (c) audit record for every fallback event.
- Contract: Fallback that permits cross-border routing is an opt-in clause with a 30-day activation window. If you require guaranteed EU-only processing even under constrained conditions, we offer reserved capacity (Dedicated) with an SLA and capacity commitment.

Next steps: I attached an EU dataflow diagram and the region attestation PDF. Ben, can you confirm how a temporary cache-only exception would be reflected in Marketplace/SOW language and what lead time we should propose? Stephanie, please flag any compliance documentation we should include for Meditech's legal team.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.company
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood_region_attestation_q3_2027.pdf, eu-dataflow-diagram.png

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
To: vanessa_ortiz; Anna Müller; Meditech Procurement
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: EU residency + temporary APAC processing allowance

Anna, Vanessa — quick commercial clarifiers:
- For the temporary APAC cache exception we typically capture this as a Rider to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) scoped to non-sensitive workloads.
- Lead time: 10 business days to operationalize once Meditech signs the Rider and provides the opt-in configuration list.
- Pricing: No additional per-token surcharge for ephemeral cache routing; if you later need cross-region dedicated capacity we will propose a Dedicated pool commitment.

I'll prepare proposed Rider language and attach a one-page summary for legal.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, EMEA | Redwood Inference

From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@meditech.eu>
To: vanessa_ortiz; ben_carter; Meditech Procurement
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 14:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Question: EU residency + temporary APAC processing allowance

Thanks — that helps. A couple follow-ups from security:
- Can you confirm the retention policy for request-level audit logs tied to ephemeral cache events? We need 7 years for logs (redacted as needed) for our internal compliance.
- For the attestation PDF, can you point to the exact controls that prevent persisted outputs from being accidentally written to APAC when fallback triggers? A brief engineer note would be helpful.

If both answers are OK we can accept the Rider model and proceed to SOW.

Best,
Anna

---
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.company>
To: Anna Müller; vanessa_ortiz; ben_carter
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: EU residency + temporary APAC processing allowance

Anna — short answers while we prepare the legal artifacts:
- Audit logs: We retain request-level audit logs for 7 years by default for Enterprise accounts with retention settings configurable via the Console. Logs are hashed/anonymized per your data classification and can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket (or customer-managed KMS). We will annotate the Rider to reference the export flow.
- Preventing accidental persistence: The runtime enforces write-policy separation. Persisted outputs are always bound to the tenant's configured persistent storage bucket in the EU region (RBAC enforced). During fallback, only transient compute and ephemeral caches are allowed to route out-of-region; a runtime guard prevents write tokens from being used to write to non-EU persistent buckets. Engineering will provide a short control note for your security team within 48 hours.

I'll loop in engineering and legal to draft the Rider & SOW language. Vanessa/Ban please share the one-page commercial for procurement.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
